claims.explanation: Didanosine is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor that also inhibits mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma and is activated by purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP). Cancer cell lines with high PNP expression or loss of mitochondrial DNA repair may be more sensitive to didanosine due to increased conversion to its active metabolite and enhanced mitochondrial toxicity. Conversely, high expression of ABC transporters or robust nucleotide salvage pathways could protect cells by reducing intracellular drug levels or compensating for mitochondrial dysfunction.

features.basis: PNP activates didanosine by phosphorolysis; high expression increases active metabolite
Damaging mutations in mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma impair repair, enhancing didanosine-induced mitochondrial toxicity
Efflux transporter reduces intracellular didanosine concentration
Nucleoside transporter uptake increases intracellular didanosine
Equilibrative nucleoside transporter facilitates didanosine entry
Deoxycytidine kinase phosphorylates didanosine to its active monophosphate
Cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase dephosphorylates and inactivates didanosine metabolites
Thymidine phosphorylase may contribute to didanosine activation or alter nucleotide pools
Loss of p53-mediated DNA damage response increases sensitivity to nucleoside analogs
Homologous recombination deficiency impairs repair of didanosine-induced DNA damage
Defective ATM signaling reduces DNA damage checkpoint, enhancing cytotoxicity
One-carbon metabolism supports nucleotide synthesis, compensating for didanosine effects
